Here’s a concise profile of Million Manhoef as of my knowledge up to late 2024:

Basic info
- Name: Million Manhoef
- Date of birth: 3 January 2002
- Nationality: Dutch (of Surinamese descent)
- Height: roughly 1.73 m (5'8")
- Position: Winger/attacking wide player; has also been used as a wing-back
- Foot: Primarily right-footed

Club career
- Youth development: Came through Vitesse’s academy system in Arnhem.
- Vitesse (senior debut 2020): Broke into the first team as a teenager. Over the next few seasons he became a regular, valued for pace, direct dribbling, chance creation, and high work rate. Under certain coaches he was also deployed as a right wing-back, which broadened his defensive responsibilities and pressing habits.
- Move to England: Transferred to Stoke City (EFL Championship) in the January 2024 window on a long-term deal (fee officially undisclosed). Brought in to add dynamism and 1v1 threat to Stoke’s wide areas.

International
- Netherlands youth international: Represented the Netherlands at multiple youth levels (various age groups). Eligible for Suriname through heritage but has been involved with Dutch youth setups.

Playing style and strengths
- Explosive first step and acceleration; likes to drive at defenders and attack space.
- Most natural as a winger on either flank; often operates off the left to cut inside onto his right.
- Comfortable receiving to feet or running in behind; good at carrying the ball through pressure.
- End product (goals/assists) trended upward in his later Vitesse seasons.
- Defensive work rate above average for an attacking wide player due to experience as a wing-back.
- Versatile: can play left wing, right wing, second striker/inside forward, and cover at wing-back in certain systems.

Background
- Family: He is the son of renowned Surinamese-Dutch kickboxer and MMA fighter Melvin Manhoef.
- Personality/traits often noted by coaches: competitive edge, willingness to press, and resilience.

Notable context
- Emerged at Vitesse during a period when the club relied on academy talent; was seen as one of their key prospects to make the jump abroad.
- The move to Stoke City in 2024 was viewed as a step to test himself in a more physical, fast-paced league and to continue developing end product and consistency.

If you want, I can pull together his latest season-by-season stats, positions played most often, or notable matches since joining Stoke (to the extent available up to 2024).
